title: Design-Robust Sup-Norm CATE Estimation under a Global Propensity Tail Envelope
banked_reason: F3 proof loop exceeded 60 iterations with three main theorem proofs incomplete; F3.5, F4, and F5 did not run.
gap_reasons: PROOF-REVIEW LOOP ESCALATION [bank-partial]: loop exceeded 60 iterations
proof_attempt_summary: The discovery graph passed D0.5 at field tier, and the formalization proved the hostile-design Rayleigh limit plus many estimator and counting helpers. F3 exhausted its 60-iteration proof loop with three real sorries in finite-bandwidth, unknown-tail adaptation, and CATE rate. F3.5, F4, and F5 did not run; the mathematical claims were not refuted, and the run is marked retryable.
tldr: A global lower-tail restriction on the treatment propensity limits how many poorly treated regions can coexist but permits arbitrary within-cell treated concentration.  Under the exact whole-space \(\mathcal H^\beta(L)\) convention, the order-\(m\) Taylor polynomial of the supplied ambient extension gives an \(O(Lh^\beta)\) approximation in every cell, including boundary cells.  Fixed polynomial-norming subcells then stabilize each occupied balanced Gram matrix.  Ordering their minimum treated masses and integrating binomial tails, with empty cells retained, gives the log-free expected sup-norm rate \(n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d\gamma/(\gamma-1))}\).  The count-admissible finite-grid selector uses neither \(\gamma\) nor \(C\) and attains this same rate for every fixed compatible tail class.  A bounded binary-outcome construction supplies the matching converse, and the smooth-control subclass gives the corresponding CATE rate.
gap: Dorn's Theorem 1 obtains the log-free weak-overlap sup-norm frontier under a local nonconcentration assumption and explicitly leaves a degeneracy-robust estimator outside scope. A global propensity-tail envelope alone does not imply that assumption.
fill: Balanced polynomial-norming subcells replace stochastic raw-design conditioning by deterministic geometry. An ordered-mass inequality then converts the single global tail budget into a summable collection of local count tails, producing a same-class upper bound and bounded-outcome converse.
